title: [Advice + Playtest] How I built a full browser 4X Hexwardia with Grok & Gemini without burning out my token budget (and how to stop LLMs from over-patching) + Thanks!
author: Antique_Pair_140

comments.author: odragora
comments.body:
Nice game with a complete gameplay loop.

I even managed to lose to those high elves warmongers after the expensive transition to Knights.

Congrats!

replies.author: Antique_Pair_140
replies.body:
Thanks a lot for playing! You're honestly the very first player in the wild I don't personally know, and I'm super glad you liked it!

If anything else comes to mind about the game—good or bad—please feel free to share. I'd love to hear both the positive and negative parts so I can go into war mode to balance things and crush bugs!

replies.author: odragora
replies.body:
I'd highly recommend taking a look at the Yield! Fall of Rome:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1561960/Yield_Fall_of_Rome/

It seems like you are sharing pretty much the exact same subgenre, and in my opinion this is one of the best games there. Maybe you'll find something interesting or inspirational for your project in it.

For example, I think they did a great job with the city development mechanic, perhaps something inspired by that could find a place in your game. Right now to me it feels like the terrain is mostly a decorative element regarding city management and development, that barely has an impact on decision making or identity of cities.

Unit types don't feel intuitive to me. I didn't get an impression that they have noticeably different purposes, roles or associated powerspikes. They are much more noticeable in Yield!. 

Another game that does that great is Age of Empires 4, where the units belong to a multi-dimensional counter system. There are Armored / Light / Ranged / Melee / Infantry / Cavalry tags, and most units deal 2x-3x damage vs one of them, and receive that from some of the units as well. So you have to use mixed unit compositions and constantly transition between them, trying to counter the composition of the opponent. Most civs unlock armored and anti-armor units only at specific tech tier (age), but some civs have earlier versions. Maybe you could find that interesting for your game.

The tile sprites do their job in terms of readability, but the game could probably benefit from a visual rework of the map to make it look more like an aesthetically pleasing game world and less like a collection of individual tiles. Adjusting the map generation to make the world more believable, like chains of mountains, rivers, lakes, forests, plains, etc, would probably also help.

Best things about my experience with the game were the AI player being able to provide challenge once it gets rolling; decently comfortable and aesthetically pleasing UI; and the overall technical and UX quality of the game, since I haven't encountered any bugs or frustrating things during my time with the game, despite it being quite ambitious for an indie project.

replies.author: Antique_Pair_140
replies.body:
Thanks a lot for the detailed breakdown, this is awesome feedback!

I checked out *Yield!*—really cool game and I love what they did with cities and tech. My main goal with Hexwardia is keeping matches quick (under 25–30 min) in a browser tab without heavy menu management, at start even resources was auto managed, but I 100% agree that surrounding terrain should shape town identity more, in future with smaler town influence circles towns will need to specialize, at last it is plan somewhere in my mind 🤔 ... 

Also totally agree on unit roles. I don't want them to just be stat upgrades, so I've already started adding soft counters (like archers vs flying) and making armor/HP and positioning (Dwarves on mountains, Elves in forests) matter much more. But being a one-man show is hard to spread over so many fronts—as of right now, I spent all day just fixing translation mistakes in 3 languages haha!

Super glad to hear the AI put up a real fight and that you didn't run into any bugs. Thanks again for taking the time to write this out, you gave me a lot of great points to check out!
